Tara — thanks for the note and the schedule. Draft MAP attached (Redwood-MAP-v2.xlsx) and a short SOW stub (Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf). High level summary below and proposed owners/dates so your procurement team can slot this into your PO cycle.

Proposed mutual action plan (summary):
1) Eval kickoff (week 0): Redwood provides test credentials, SE onboarding, and 2-week proof-of-concept (PoC). Owner: Marissa Cole. Target: 2028-12-18.
2) Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence (concurrent with PoC): Redwood to supply SOC2 type II report excerpts, data handling docs, and optional on-prem config notes. Owner: Laura Bennett. Target: 2028-12-22.
3) Technical validation & perf baseline (during PoC): Redwood SE provides perf runbooks (latency/cost guides) and assists with 2 sample workloads. Owner: Marissa. Target: 2028-12-29.
4) Procurement & legal review: AurumTech to share standard PO terms; Redwood to propose private offer terms (AWS/Azure/GCP). Owner: Jonas + AurumTech procurement. Target kickoff: 2029-01-04; aim to finalize PO by 2029-01-18.
5) Marketplace private offer creation & acceptance: Once terms agreed, Redwood initiates private offer (AWS preferred per your note). Billing path choices:
   - AWS Private Offer: charge goes through AWS invoicing (Marketplace billing) with Redwood as the seller of record; requires buyer marketplace account ID and PO flow through AWS.
   - Direct invoice: Redwood invoices AurumTech directly under a standard monthly usage invoice (preferred for some enterprise finance teams).
   We’ll capture the choice in the MAP and model sample invoices for underwriting.
6) Post-accept rollout: Reserved capacity or dedicated pool activation, onboarding plan and SLO commitments. Owner: Jonas + Redwood Ops. Target: 2029-02-01.

Key attachments included: Redwood-MAP-v2.xlsx (MAP with milestone column, owners, gate criteria), Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf (3-page SOW stub), plus a quick link to an example AWS private offer flow.

Open questions for procurement/legal (please confirm):
- Does AurumTech require payment to be handled via AWS Marketplace, or do you prefer Redwood direct invoicing?
- Are there any SOC2 or data residency artifacts beyond the standard report you need for the legal packet?
- Any internal PO number or commitment window we should reference for the private offer (your Q1 commit code)?

Next steps: If this looks reasonable, Marissa will schedule the technical kickoff and I’ll coordinate a short call next Tuesday to align procurement/legal owners.

Tara — quick note from the SE side. I added technical acceptance criteria into the MAP (see row: perf baselines + sample prompt set). A couple technical clarifications to make the PoC efficient: 
- We’ll need a 20–50k token sample workload and two representative datasets (anonymized) to run latency/cost baselines — can you confirm where those live?
- If AurumTech wants dedicated capacity during rollout we’ll include reserved pool sizing in the SOW (estimated GPU-hours per month).

Also: for the private offer, the AWS path requires your AWS account alias and marketplace buyer ID to be provided to create a seller-initiated private offer. If AurumTech is leaning Azure instead we can do the equivalent but there are small billing differences (invoice cadence and price-display behavior).

I’ve copied Karthik to confirm procurement-side playbook (he helps with marketplace acceptance cadence). Karthik — can you confirm typical time-to-accept once buyer procurement provides PO + marketplace account ID?
